stories.title: Budget tax measures pass despite opposition criticism
stories.summary: The Dáil last night passed a number of tax measures to give effect to changes announced in yesterday's Budget. The Taoiseach told a meeting of the Fianna Fáil parliamentary party in Leinster House that income tax changes and cuts to childcare costs would be a big help to households. However, opposition parties have been trenchant in their criticism of the Budget saying it fell short of what was required to tackle the rising cost of living. An additional €5,000 in the Help-to-Buy scheme for those purchasing their first homes along with a €1 excise duty hike on a packet of 20 cigarettes were among the budget changes passed in the Dáil. There was criticism from some opposition parties over the Help-to-Buy increase, saying it would only push up the price of homes. Cuts to the carbon tax on home heating oil and gas, along with the extension of excise duty reductions on petrol and diesel until the end of February, were also voted through.

stories.title: Ryder Cup captains in Limerick hope to 'inspire' juniors
stories.summary: The captains of the European and US Ryder Cup teams have visited a Limerick golf course where the focus is firmly on the next generation, as the countdown to next year's tournament at Adare Manor continues. Luke Donald and Jim Furyk were at Rathbane Golf Course, in one of Limerick city’s regeneration areas, to meet young golfers and highlight the opportunities the sport can offer beyond the elite level. While Adare Manor will host the world’s best players next year, Rathbane has spent almost three decades making golf accessible and affordable to people of all ages and abilities. Thousands have taken their first steps into the sport on the fairways of the municipal course, and the hope is that the Ryder Cup will inspire many more to follow. European captain Luke Donald said major events like the Ryder Cup had an important role to play in encouraging young people to take up the game. "This is how you grow the game and inspire juniors to love the game like I did," he said. "I certainly watched some Ryder Cups when I was growing up and that was very inspirational for me.

stories.title: INTO announces second strike date over public pay deal
stories.summary: The General Secretary of the Irish National Teachers' Organisation, John Boyle, has said that a second strike day set for 21 October is going ahead. Members of the INTO and the Association of Secondary Teachers Ireland (ASTI) commenced industrial action today in the form of a work-to-rule over delays in securing a new pay agreement. More than 100,000 public sector workers began industrial action last week ahead of a planned strike on 14 October. "And the decisions out of those meetings is that the strike that was indicated for the 21st of October will now also be going ahead." Unions have accused the Government of failing to make meaningful commitments on pay following the expiration of the last public sector pay deal on 30 June. Action today by INTO members in some primary schools led to disruptions to early drop-offs and late collections outside of school hours.

stories.title: Cybersecurity experts from across Europe gather in Dublin
stories.summary: A major cybersecurity conference is being held in Dublin as part of Ireland's EU Presidency. The National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) will host the event at a time of heightened concerns about the impact of artificial intelligence (AI) on cybersecurity. In recent months, there has been a series of reports of rogue AI agents hacking systems. Today's conference will hear from representatives from tech companies such as OpenAI and Anthropic. Other speakers include senior representatives from government, EU institutions, academia and the wider European cybersecurity community. The conference will explore the rapidly evolving cybersecurity landscape, with a strong focus on European cyber resilience, security and competitiveness.

stories.title: Yemen's Houthis claim new attack on Riyadh airport
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthis have claimed an attack on the main airport in the Saudi capital while also denying losing territory to government forces, as fighting intensified. After declaring a counter-offensive, government forces claimed yesterday to have pushed the Houthis out of the Bab al-Mandab area, a key shipping route in the Red Sea, as well as the port city of Mocha, which was captured last month. Claims by both sides have been impossible to independently verify with the situation on the ground moving fast and access for journalists difficult. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree claimed on Telegram that the group still held all territory recently seized, including strategic areas along the Red Sea coast. Their fighters "have full control over all their advances on the ground", he said. He said the Houthis had carried out dozens of strikes in the past few hours targeting government forces in Yemen's Al-Jawf and Marib regions, while also attacking Taiz governorate.

stories.title: Mustaki wants total focus to avoid Astana 'banana skin'
stories.summary: Chloe Mustaki was "buzzing" after the Republic of Ireland were pitted against Kazakhstan in the World Cup play-offs but admits her enthusiasm has been tempered by a long trek to Central Asia and a realisation that the minnows are seriously fired up to cause an upset. The Kazakhs (98th in the world) were the lowest ranked side Ireland possibly could have met in the play-off semi-finals. Carla Ward's Girls in Green are up to 21st following an excellent qualification campaign that saw them beat Poland (twice) and the Netherlands. There's no doubt it was a kind draw, but it's also a logistical challenge: a 10-and-a-half-hour flight, freezing temperatures and the Astana Arena's artificial pitch will take Ireland out of their comfort zone. The absence of Katie McCabe (suspended) and Denise O'Sullivan (rested) also deprives Ward of two elite game-changers. The message over the last few days in camp has been clear: there's zero room for complacency. "I remember listening to the draw in the summer, I was on holidays at the time, and I was absolutely buzzing that we got Kazakhstan initially just based off the ranking," said Mustaki, who continues to shine for Nottingham Forest in WSL2. "But then looking into the journey and obviously now having looked at how they play and the type of opposition that they are, it's been more of a challenge than initially expected.

stories.title: Kinnerk and Currid set to remain with Limerick in 2027
stories.summary: Limerick hurling coach Paul Kinnerk is set to stay put with the defending All-Ireland champions in 2027, with manager John Kiely confirming that his backroom staff are set to remain in place. Kiely was previously proposed for an 11th season in charge following their 2026 triumph, with confirmation from the county board expected later this month. Kinnerk and performance psychologist Caroline Currid are both staying put, as are John Flavin, Alan Cunningham, Liam Cronin and Donal O'Grady who were selectors and coaches last season. Speaking to the Limerick Leader on Monday, Kiely said the decision comes after a period of reflection following their Liam MacCarthy Cup win in July. "We had to have a bit of reflection to see what was the best thing to do going forward," said Kiely. "We've obviously committed to going forward again for 2027 and we're very much looking forward to that.

stories.title: Crawford's U21s ready for down-to-the-wire scenario
stories.summary: Jim Crawford says Ireland are prepared for every eventuality as they head into this evening's final-day showdown against England (6pm) with a European Under-21 Championship play-off spot on the line. The Boys in Green hold the all-important second spot in Group D, but only a victory over Lee Carsley’s Young Lions, who are already qualified as table-toppers, will guarantee their progression. Failing that, Ireland would require Slovakia to slip up in Andorra. Both sides are tied on 17 points, but Ireland possess the head-to-head tiebreaker. This down-to-the-wire scenario at a sold-out Turner’s Cross looked unlikely after Crawford’s side were humbled 4-0 by the Pyrenean microstate, but three consecutive wins have put them in control of their own destiny. Andorra remain unbeaten at home in this group (two wins, two draws) and were only denied a famous victory over England by a 90th-minute Rico Lewis penalty. Still, Crawford isn’t expecting any favours. "The unfortunate thing is that Andorra, when they played against us, they dropped down quite a few first-team players. I don't think that's going to happen against Slovakia," he said.

stories.title: Frawley and O'Shea add greater lustre to out-half debate
stories.summary: It was a tale of two Irish out-halves in last weekend's United Rugby Championship matches. Ciarán Frawley made the best first impression possible at his new club, guiding Connacht to victory over Benetton in Italy with a late try to seal the win. It is a dream start for the former Leinster utility back who has made the less conventional move west to prove a point to many people, including the Irish coaches and his former mentors at Leinster. Frawley is a talented footballer. It’s the reason he got caught in the dreaded utility role. He was so good at covering multiple positions that he never quite nailed down a sustained opportunity to make the number 10 jersey his own. When he did get his chance to perform in his preferred jersey, he had some sublime moments, mixed with some periods where he under performed. It’s not surprising that when a player in a key position fails to get enough game-time in a game management position, he fails to perform to the required level on the international stage. Though it didn’t stop him from converting a pair of memorable drop goals to beat South Africa in their own back yard. Frawley has a sizeable frame. That's why he can perform at centre and full-back. His size allows him to be a real attacking threat, taking the ball as close to the tackle line as any of the best Irish attacking out-halves. His decision making in traffic is helped by his ability to manage himself in contact. When he’s confident, there’s venom in his attacking style.

stories.title: Something For The Weekend: Declan O'Rourke's cultural picks
stories.summary: Declan O'Rourke’s eighth studio LP, Oceanic, is his first release since a triumphant series of sell-out shows earlier this year celebrating the celebrating 20 years of his debut album Since Kyabram. Recorded in Australia, where he made his first recordngs aged 19, the album carries a particular resonance, drawing a line between where O’Rourke first began and where he now stands creatively.. Recently watched and loved Werckmeister Harmonies. A brilliant Hungarian film. Watch out for Almost With You, which premiered at the Galway Film Fleadh recently and will be out next year. My new record, Oceanic, comes out October 16th! We’ve released three single slash videos so far. Echo, For Free, and Earl Grey And Edwin. Check them out! I’ve been told recently that Donal O’Kelly’s play Catalpa is great. But it’s not running at the moment. Perhaps he should put it back on, given the very significant anniversary!

stories.title: Eccleston praises community spirit on Irish film set
stories.summary: Christopher Eccleston and Madeleine Madden have spoken about the sense of community they experienced while filming Chasing Millions in Dublin and Dundalk. Directed by Stephen Burke, the upcoming movie takes inspiration from the 2004 Northern Bank robbery in Belfast, when £26 million was stolen in what became one of the biggest bank robberies in British and Irish history. But rather than telling the story as a conventional crime thriller, Burke has taken a character-driven and darkly comic approach to the aftermath of the robbery, setting the story against a Northern Ireland still coming to terms with the legacy of the Troubles. Eccleston plays veteran Northern Irish detective Crayford, while Australian actor Madden plays Diana, an ambitious young Australian police officer who becomes determined to solve the case. Although the story is set in Belfast, much of the film was shot in Dublin and Dundalk. For Eccleston and Madden, one of the most memorable parts of the production was the response from the communities where they were filming. "When we were shooting the scene where Chris gets out of the car and confronts the kids and got the fake money, it was just so wonderful. Even in Dublin too, when we were shooting these exterior scenes, in some of the suburbs and neighbourhoods the whole community came out."

stories.title: Ceremony to mark four years since Creeslough explosion
stories.summary: A commemoration service will take place in Creeslough, Co Donegal, this afternoon to mark the fourth anniversary of the explosion in which ten people died. The explosion at a service station and apartment complex on 7 October 2022 claimed the lives of four men, three women and three children, ranging in age from five to 59. They were five-year-old Shauna-Flanagan Garwe and her 50-year-old father Robert Garwe, 14-year-old Leona Harper, 59-year-old Hugh Kelly, 24-year-old Jessica Gallagher, 49-year-old Martin McGill, 48-year-old James O'Flaherty, 49-year-old Martina Martin, 39-year-old Catherine O'Donnell and her 13-year-old son James Monaghan. Family members and friends are expected to lay wreaths this afternoon at the site of the explosion, while local clergy are expected to offer prayers in memory of those who died. Gardaí are continuing to carry out an investigation into the explosion in conjunction with the Health and Safety Authority and the Commission for the Regulation of Utilities. A file was sent to the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions in September 2025, and a supplementary file was sent in April which included formal recommendations.

stories.title: Funding to recruit 1,000 gardaí, bringing force to 15,000
stories.summary: The Minister for Public Expenditure and Reform has said he is allocating funding to recruit up to 1,000 trainee gardaí, bringing the force to over 15,000 next year. In today's Budget speech, Jack Chambers also announced a package of €1.6 billion for the Department of Defence, an increase of almost 9%. This will provide for 850 new permanent Defence Force members as well as increases for Air Corps and naval service equipment. National Development Plan funding of €340 million will also support the new delivery of new helicopters and the military radar programme, the minister stated. That funding will also support investment in maritime surveillance and cyber security, as well as the modernisation and upgrade of military installations throughout the country. Mr Chambers said gardaí play a critical role in ensuring people around the country remain safe.

stories.title: Bill for Govt hosting EU Presidency rises to over €75m
stories.summary: The bill to the Government is hosting the six-month EU Presidency to the end of August totals €75.2 million. That is according to new figures provided by the Minister for Public Expenditure, Infrastructure, Public Service Reform and Digitalisation, Jack Chambers. In the figures provided in a written Dáil reply to Independent Ireland TD Ken O'Flynn , Minister Chambers reveals that the largest spend by any Department to date has been €26.3m by the Dept of Justice, Home Affairs and Migration. Ireland commenced hosting the EU Presidency on 1 July, and garda overtime would account for the largest portion of the Department of Justice spend, where Minister Chambers further disclosed that the Dept of Foreign Affairs spend on the EU Presidency to the end of August was €20.3m. The bulk of the spend has been made by the two Government Departments along with the Office of Public Works (OPW), which has spent €19.6m on the EU Presidency to the end of August. In his written Dáil reply, Minister Chambers stated that revised Government Estimates 2026 allocated €300m to cover the costs of hosting the EU Presidency.

stories.title: Porsche braces for lower sales era, seeks luxury lifeline
stories.summary: Porsche is steeling itself for persistently lower sales, the Volkswagen brand said today, pitching a turnaround plan to investors that aims to boost margins with a focus on top-end models. The sports car maker, like parent Volkswagen, is undergoing restructuring to address weak demand and high costs. It said it would lower its future break-even point to fewer than 200,000 units, compared with total deliveries last year of 279,449. Porsche has already seen deliveries slump by almost 10% globally since the year of its blockbuster listing in 2022, as plunging demand in China and tariff woes in the US hit two of the brand's most important markets. During a capital markets day at the company's development centre in Weissach, CEO Michael Leiters will seek to assure investors that a focus on high-end sports cars like the 911 and luxury SUVs will put the carmaker back on track. Its profit margin collapsed last year to 1.1%, a fraction of the double-digit, Ferrari-style margins targeted when the Stuttgart-based carmaker went public four years ago under Oliver Blume, Leiters' predecessor.

stories.title: Proposals over EU policies for future candidate countries
stories.summary: Future EU candidate countries will have to more strictly align with the bloc's policies ahead of joining in the wake of persistent rule of law conflicts between recent arrivals, such as Hungary, and established member states, according to new plans proposed by the European Commission. Under the proposals, which will require the consent of member states, there will be stricter safeguards before a candidate country joins the European Union in order to avoid democratic backsliding once the applicant joins. The EU is preparing to take in countries such as Montenegro, Albania, Ukraine and Moldova in the coming years while trying to reassure existing members about potential political and economic costs. The renewed emphasis on enlargement, which the Irish Government strongly supports, is a response to Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine and Kyiv’s desire to join the bloc as part of a peace settlement. Under the new measures, other EU countries could be able to suspend a new member's voting rights during the first 15 years of membership if it stops adhering to the bloc’s values. There is also a plan to limit financial support for Ukraine’s large farming sector, particularly its grain economy.

stories.title: Duffy: 'We've had our downs - we've turned it around'
stories.summary: Nearing the end of a turbulent campaign, Derry City look to have found their form in time to mount another tilt for FAI Cup glory, with Galway United standing in the way of a third final appearance in the 2020s. In a stark reminder of what a chaotic and messy season it had been for Derry for so long, their pre-semi-final press conference was preceded by the appearance of a PFAI press release issued on behalf of James McClean, in which the Republic of Ireland centurion hit out at his "incomprehensible" treatment from his hometown club. The statement evidently caught Derry City by surprise, the club pointedly noting in their response that "it was made without prior notice to the club, just four days before the biggest match of the club's season." Interim manager Mark Connolly, who has not selected McClean for any competitive match-day squads since his appointment in early August, said he had just seen the statement for the first time this morning and wasn't inclined to comment publicly on the matter. "Obviously, I've seen it this morning when we were heading into training," Connolly said. "James had acknowledged that he didn't want to be a public thing and that's the way I work. We just want to keep everything in-house and my full focus is on Saturday's game."

stories.summary: As newly appointed Galway football manager Éamonn Fitzmaurice settles into his first full week in the job, his former Kerry team-mate Mike Quirke believes it could be the start of an 'exciting time' for the Tribesmen. Fitzmaurice was officially appointed as Padraic Joyce's successor last week on a three-year term and will now look to guide his new charges to a first All-Ireland crown since 2001. The ex-Kerry boss is returning to the inter-county game after an absence of eight seasons, having stepped down as Kingdom manager following the conclusion of the 2018 championship. During his six years in charge, Fitzmaurice helped Kerry to the 2014 All-Ireland title, having collected three Celtic Crosses during his playing career - including one at Galway's expense in 2000. Quirke - who also spent time as part of an All-Ireland winning Kerry management team in 2022 - says that it looks like a natural move for the Finuge clubman. "Éamonn has obviously been out of the game at senior inter-county level for a number of years, he obviously was so embedded in the FRC and looking at the rules and through his media stuff then as well had a really close connection with the game.

stories.summary: Argentina, Uruguay, Chile and Brazil have submitted a joint bid to host the Rugby World Cup in 2035, hoping to bring the quadrennial tournament to ⁠South America for the first time. The bid outlines plans to stage games in 11 stadiums across 10 cities, with eight venues in Argentina and one each in the other three countries, including the iconic Maracana in Rio de Janeiro. Spain and Japan have also expressed interest in hosting the tournament. World Rugby will undertake site visits and feasibility ‌assessments before identifying a ⁠preferred host by next May, with a final decision expected in November 2027. "We have the opportunity to show the world our passion for this sport, our ability to host major events, and everything our countries have to offer," Argentine Rugby Union (UAR) president Felix Paez ‌Molina said in a statement. "We take on this challenge firmly believing that our region deserves an opportunity of ⁠this size. "It's a project we're excited about, and we're building it ‌together with the region's Unions and Sudamerica Rugby. Our hope is ⁠that, for ‌the first time, a Rugby World Cup can be played in this part of the world."

stories.title: Culture and Budget 2026 - everything you need to know
stories.summary: The Department of Culture, Communications and Sport will receive a package of €1.3 billion, Minster Chambers announced today. Within that budget, Minister Chambers confirmed that €34.4 million will provide a full year of income support for artists, saying that it will help artists "to remain in creative work." The Minister stated that the budget would provide "record funding for The Arts Council". It will be increased by €2.5 million from its current allocation of €140 million to €142.5 million. This increase will be welcomed by the organisation, as it begins a new chapter with the recent announcement of the appointment of a new director, Shona McCarthy for a five year term. The Minister confirmed a budget allocation of "almost €89 million support to national cultural institutions" with an increase of €3.8 million, and he also stated that funding "will be provided for the Fleadh Ceoil" which will return to Belfast in 2027, after a hugely successful event during the summer of 2026.

stories.title: Freddie Jackson, Grammy-nominated R&B singer, dies at 70
stories.summary: US musician Freddie Jackson, known for songs such as You Are My Lady and Rock Me Tonight (For Old Times Sake), has been remembered as a "legendary voice" after his death aged 70. The singer, who was born in New York City, was renowned for his smooth 1980s hits and achieved 10 number one singles on the Billboard R&B charts during his decades-long career, along with two Grammy nods. His family revealed with "profound sadness and heavy hearts" that their "beloved" Freddie had died on Monday night, in a post shared to his Instagram page the following day. It read: "Freddie was more than a legendary voice. He was a kind, generous soul who loved his fans, his family, his friends, and his music with everything he had. "For decades he gave us the songs that became the soundtrack to our love stories, our celebrations, and our most treasured memories. That gift will live on forever. "To everyone who ever sang along, danced, or felt something when Freddie took the stage: thank you. You were family to him, and he carried your love with him always."

stories.title: How to make your bed the cosiest it can be for winter
stories.summary: Francis Brennan, television personality and hotelier, joined Drivetime to share his advice on turning your bed into the perfect serene sanctuary ahead of winter. Listen back above. There's nothing like curling up in your bed at the end of a long day, but when the temperature drops you want to make sure your bed is especially cosy. Transitioning from an exceptionally hot summer can be challenging, esepcially when getting to sleep in the last few months has involved throwing off the duvet, opening all windows and maybe buying a bedroom fan. But with a few small additions to your bedding, you can bank plenty of restful sleep. "The first thing is your mattress", Brennan says. "You have to pay attention to your mattress. There's no point putting the best of everything on top of a very bad mattress." Making sure you're looking after your mattress is crucial, he adds: "You should turn your mattress at least - at least - once every six months, and when I say turn I don't mean swing around on the same side. I mean turn it over so that your side goes over the other side and his side comes over your side." Doing this prevents the mattress developing dips from sleeping on the same side or sitting on it to tie shoe laces.

stories.title: Israel marks three years since deadly Hamas attack
stories.summary: Israelis will mark three years since Hamas attacked Israel on 7 October, 2023, triggering ⁠a military assault that destroyed much of Gaza, where conditions remain dire despite a year-old ceasefire that is meant to halt the war for good. The attacks, during which militants killed 1,200 people and took 251 hostages to Gaza, marked the deadliest day in Israel's history. Israel's subsequent bombardment and ground operations have killed more than 74,000 people in Gaza, Hamas-run health authorities there say. At the site of the Nova music festival, where 348 people were killed, family members bowed their heads at 6.29am (4.29am Irish time), surrounded by portraits of victims with flowers placed underneath. A memorial event will also be held later at Hostage Square in Tel Aviv. The anniversary is the first for Israelis without any hostages still held in Gaza, with those dead and alive exchanged in swaps with Hamas for Palestinians held in Israeli jails.

stories.title: €10 Social Welfare rise 'simply not enough' - TD
stories.summary: Weekly Social Welfare rates, including Jobseeker's Allowance and pensions, will rise by €10. In Budget 2027, a new cost of disability payment worth €500 a year has also been announced. Other measures will see the Carer's Allowance income disregard increased to €1,150 for a single person and €2,300 for a couple. The Weekly Fuel Allowance rate will increase by €5, while the income threshold for single pensioners will rise from €534 to €641 per week. Social Justice Ireland said the €10 core Social Welfare rate failed to compensate for "the damage that inflation continues to wreak on poorer households". Labour's Social Protection Spokesperson Mark Wall said the additional €10 for Social Welfare is "not a win".

stories.title: Two factors preventing ministers from budget utopia
stories.summary: Rarely has so much cash coalesced with such levels of political angst. These are not the days of austerity when the late Brian Lenihan pledged that swingeing cuts would allow the country to turn the proverbial corner. However, two complicating factors are preventing ministers from entering budget utopia. This first is rising energy costs, followed closely by soaring grocery bills. That presents the seemingly strange scenario where the country is getting richer, but households are watching their disposable income shrink. Obviously, the Budget, which will be unveiled on Tuesday, must leave workers and families feeling that they were helped.

stories.title: Indian central bank hikes rates for first time since 2023
stories.summary: India's central bank hiked interest rates today for the first time since 2023 as the Middle East conflict stokes inflation in Asia's third-largest economy and batters a weakened rupee. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) said the benchmark repurchase rate, the level at which it lends to commercial banks, would be raised by 25 basis points to 5.5% after a unanimous vote by a six-member panel. In doing so, the Reserve Bank of India shifted gears to join several central banks around the world who have raised rates to curb price rises or boost their currencies. Since the outbreak of the Iran war in February, the Reserve Bank of India has stood pat as it waited to assess the impact of volatile oil prices on the world's fastest-growing major economy. But resilient GDP growth last quarter has allowed it to focus on higher costs in a country that imports most of its energy and has been hit by a weak monsoon that could result in a spike in food prices. Retail inflation rose to 4.8% in August - the third month in a row that headline inflation breached the Reserve Bank of India's medium term target of 4% - with data signalling that inflationary pressures had spread beyond food and transport.

stories.title: Massive drone attack kills two in Moscow
stories.summary: Hundreds of drones hit Moscow overnight, killing two men on the outskirts of the capital and injuring nine others, Russian authorities have said. Overnight, "650 drones were launched toward the Moscow region", Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said on Telegram, stressing that "most (were) destroyed by air defences at long range". Moscow Region governor Andrei Vorobyov said 185 drones were "destroyed or neutralised" overnight over 16 municipalities in the region. But he said that the attack killed two men, aged 71 and 20, in two different locations on the outskirts of Moscow, while nine others were injured. And 47 houses across seven municipalities had been damaged, as had four apartments in a residential building in the village of Lobanovo, he said. According to the Russian state news agency TASS, the pummelling was the second-largest drone attack in the past two years on the Russian capital and its surrounding region, hundreds of kilometres from the Ukrainian border.

stories.title: Caulfield wants cup run to be a springboard in Galway
stories.summary: Galway United manager John Caulfield wants to give more local fans a reason to get behind the side as preparations continue for their Club Orange Men's FAI Cup semi-final against Derry City on Saturday. A full-house is expected in Eamonn Deacy Park for the afternoon kick-off as ticket sales tick towards the marker, and for Caulfield, who has been in situ since August 2020, excitement is building ahead of a rare cup run for the Galwegians. Speaking on Monday, Caulfield emphasised a sporting "culture" in Galway that mirrors his predecessors of Cork City, and tapping into that buzz around the city. "The uniqueness is that Galway has so many sports teams as well because hurling and football is so strong," the Galway United manager said. "Connacht (rugby) in the city are strong and we have been down for a long time, but in the last three or four years we've come good. "But you can see the positivity around the place. Are the people of Galway city and county aware that Galway United are in the cup semi-final on Saturday? Absolutely. And the more times you play big matches or you can get to big occasions, that brings massive publicity to the club, brings massive positive feelings, increases your support base (and) increases your young following."
